uncited: Application-Specific Extensions adapt the standard 3D Gaussian Splatting (3DGS) framework [2812-3d-gaussian-splatting.md] to solve problems beyond novel-view synthesis of RGB images.

They address the limitations of standard 3DGS—such as its reliance on view-dependent spherical harmonics for color and its implicit volumetric representation—by modifying attribute definitions, rendering equations, or post-processing steps.
This family includes methods for physical property reconstruction (radiative/tomographic), non-photometric domain adaptation (microscopy, ultrasound), and explicit geometry extraction (meshing).

All extensions in this family retain the core 3D Gaussian primitive representation: a set of $M$ anisotropic 3D Gaussian kernels $\mathcal{G} = \{G_i\}_{i=1}^M$ [Radiative Gaussian Splatting](3040-radiative-gaussian-splatting.md).

In radiative and domain-specific variants, this is replaced by view-independent scalar attributes or feature vectors [1875-volumetric-gaussian-splatting-avis.md], [3301-gaussian-splatting-for-microscopy.md], [5170-ultragauss-rendering.md].

Originating from the need to apply Gaussian Splatting beyond standard computer graphics, these extensions emerged as the 3DGS framework [2812-3d-gaussian-splatting.md] gained traction for its efficiency.

The divergence from photometric rendering began with adaptations for scientific imaging (X-ray, microscopy) and later expanded to explicit geometry extraction to bridge the gap between implicit splats and explicit mesh-based pipelines.
